subject: Pricing follow-up: token benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic and target $/1M tokens
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up & pricing benchmarks — target $/1M tokens

Hi Jordan,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and the next steps we agreed on:

- Scope: ACME wants to use Redwood for multi-turn generative assistants (customer support + content generation).
- Current estimate (from your comments): ~50M tokens/month initially, scaling to ~200M+ over 6-12 months depending on usage.

Attached is a short benchmarking workbook (20261205-redwood-pricing-comparative.xlsx) that shows:
- Redwood representative $/1M token tiers (hosted & committed Dedicated pricing)
- Comparable public host prices (OpenAI, Anthropic) and common open-model hosts for similar model quality
- Example unit-economics (how batching, caching, and sequence lengths affect effective $/1M)

High-level numbers from the attachment (ballpark / illustrative):
- OpenAI (comparable capability): ~$1,100 - $1,400 per 1M tokens
- Anthropic: ~$1,000 - $1,300 per 1M tokens
- Open-model hosts (varies): ~$600 - $900 per 1M tokens
- Redwood hosted: $600 per 1M tokens (list), with committed Dedicated discounts to ~$350 per 1M for larger commits and reserved capacity

Important nuance: the headline $/1M is only one lever — real unit economics depend on 1) average request length, 2) prefix reuse (how much KV cache you can re-use), 3) batching and QPS profile, and 4) the model variant. Our attached modeling shows realistic reductions of 20-40% on effective cost with prefix caching + batching.

Ask: can you confirm the expected steady-state monthly token volume range and the target $/1M you need to hit (you mentioned $/1M target on the call)? Also share any procurement constraints (term length, PO process) so we can surface committed pricing options.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- ACME to confirm target $/1M and monthly volume range (you)
- Redwood to produce 1) committed pricing options (3 / 6 / 12 month), 2) sample SOW/invoice and 3) a short note on SLA/penalties for production traffic
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with infra team if you want to validate latency/cost tradeoffs

I'll follow up with committed pricing scenarios once we have your target price and volumes.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Cc: ACME Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & pricing benchmarks — target $/1M tokens

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the detailed recap and the workbook. Quick answers from our side:

- Steady-state volume: initially ~50M tokens/month, planning for growth to 150-200M tokens/month within Q1 post-launch. Peak bursts could hit ~10-12 reqs/sec for certain flows.
- Our target: ~$500 per 1M tokens as a blended target (we recognize not all models will map exactly).
- Budget cadence: we have a monthly OPEX budget range of $20k- $35k for the first 6 months; if the economics hit the $500/1M target, we can expand that for Q2.

Procurement: standard PO required, 30-45 day payment terms. For committed pricing we typically commit to a 6-12 month minimum spend (happy to discuss caps and ramp schedule).

Can you translate the committed options into a simple MAP (mutual action plan) with milestones and draft SOW? Procurement will want the sample invoice line items and any pass-through infra/cloud fees called out.

Thanks - Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of AI Products | ACME Corp
jordan.smith@acme.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up & pricing benchmarks — target $/1M tokens

Jordan - perfect, that's exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifications and a short worked example so procurement has something concrete: 

Worked example (blended effective cost assumptions):
- Baseline: Redwood hosted list = $600 / 1M tokens (no commit)
- Committed Dedicated (example): 6 month commit that covers ~75% of steady-state usage -> effective $/1M = $350 (includes reserved capacity discount and predictable throughput)
- OpenAI comparable: ~$1,200 / 1M (public list for similar capability) - note: this is often higher for top-tier models and for chat-heavy workloads
- Anthropic comparable: ~$1,050 / 1M (public list)

How we get to your target $500 / 1M for 50M/month:
- If you commit to a 6-month reserved capacity covering ~50-75M tokens/month, we can offer $425 / 1M as the initial committed price.
- With a 12-month ramp and a spend-based rebate we can reach $350 / 1M once you hit 150M tokens/month.
- Effective monthly spend examples (rounded):
  - 50M tokens @ $425/1M = $21,250 / month (within your stated $20k- $35k)
  - 150M tokens @ $350/1M = $52,500 / month

Operational notes that affect unit economics:
- Prefix caching: if support flows reuse long prefixes (we discussed knowledge-grounded chat), effective tokens billed per session drop substantially - the workbook shows up to 30% effective savings in many setups.
- Batching and concurrency: for QPS profiles like yours we can tune semibatched paths to lower GPU overhead without hurting latency SLOs.

Next concrete items from Redwood:
1) I'll share an initial MAP and three committed pricing options (month-to-month hosted, 6-month commit, 12-month commit + ramp + rebate) by EOD tomorrow.
2) We'll include a sample invoice and a short SOW template that calls out payment terms and pass-through cloud fees.
3) If procurement needs a formal SLA table and security evidence (SOC2 + customer audit options), Marissa will own that thread and loop in security if needed.

If this looks good I'll draft the MAP with explicit milestones (kickoff, pilot, production, review) and a sample invoice line showing token pricing and any infra credits.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

I'll draft the SOW skeleton and the MAP milestones and share in the Drive folder. Vanessa - if you want I can take the first draft of the MAP so we can get it to ACME procurement quickly.
